video_caption: The video begins with a light blue background displaying "Klaus Goepel" in blue and "Business Performance Management" in faded white text. This title text then changes to a prominent dark red as a 2D graph appears, showing bars for months (Jan to Dec) on the x-axis (labeled "Business Year") and "OI YTD" on the y-axis, with lines indicating "OI plan" and "± ΔOI". The graph then dramatically transforms into a complex, warped 3D surface, revealing a table on the right with financial indicators like "CPO," "PPC," and "GMP" alongside percentage values, with "Klaus Goepel" and "Business Performance Management" persistently displayed below. This intricate 3D visualization then fades, revealing a man with short, graying hair and glasses, wearing a white collared shirt, speaking directly to the camera against a plain, light-colored wall. As he talks, red text overlays appear, stating: "When you combine individual performance indicators to one KPI, you can give each one a different weight. Now the question is: How to derive the weights? For this, a mathematical method is available called AHP." The man maintains a clear and direct gaze throughout, occasionally gesturing with his hands.

The video segment opens with a light blue background featuring two 3D rectangular boxes. The top box is dark gray with the white text "Business Performance Management", and below it is a dark blue box with the white text "Analytic Hierarchy Process". After a few seconds, the dark gray "Business Performance Management" box disappears, and the dark blue box slides up slightly, now displaying the white text "Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP)" on its main face and "Deriving ratio scales from paired comparisons." on a thinner, lighter gray layer beneath it. Subsequently, a new, light brown 3D box appears below the dark blue box, displaying "Allows some small inconsistency in judgment." in white text. This light brown box then changes to a yellow-green color and moves down, while an orange 3D box slides into view below it. This orange box contains the white text "Input: Actual measurement Subjective opinion". To its right, a light gray 3D box appears, connected by a white curly brace, and contains the white text "{ price, weight etc. satisfaction feelings, preferences". Finally, a red downward-pointing arrow emerges from the bottom of the orange "Input" box, and another orange 3D box appears below the arrow, showing the white text "Output: Ratio scales Consistency index". To the right of this "Output" box, a second light gray 3D box appears, also connected by a white curly brace, with the white text "{ from Eigen vectors from Eigen value". The overall presentation uses these animated boxes to explain key aspects of the Analytic Hierarchy Process.

The video segment displays a light blue background with a dark green rectangular bar at the top labeled "Analytic Hierarchy Process." At 0:05, an orange rectangular bar appears below it, titled "Step 1: Define Objective." This bar then transitions to grey, and a downward arrow emerges from it as a new orange bar, "Step 2: Structure elements in criteria, sub-criteria, alternatives etc.," appears below the arrow. This process repeats: the current step bar turns grey, a downward arrow appears, and the next step in an orange bar is revealed. At 0:17, "Step 3: Make a pair wise comparison of elements in each group" appears. At 0:23, "Step 4: Calculate weighting and consistency ratio" is shown. Finally, at 0:29, "Step 5: Evaluate alternatives according weighting" appears. The last step, appearing at 0:34, is a smaller orange bar at the bottom with "Get ranking," indicating the final output of the process. The text "Analytic Hierarchy Process - Example" briefly flashes over the top bar at the very end of the segment.

The video segment introduces an example of the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). It begins by stating the "Objective: Buy a gadget (smart phone, MP3 player...)" displayed in dark blue text on a lighter blue background. Next, three "Criteria:" are presented: "Color", "Memory", and "Delivery", each appearing as a separate gray block. Beneath these criteria, their respective "Sub-Criteria" are listed in orange blocks: for "Color", options are "Pink, blue, green, black, red"; for "Memory", options are "8 MB, 16 MB, 32 MB, 64 MB"; and for "Delivery", options are "Immediate, 5 days, 4 weeks". Following this, four specific "Models:" or "(Alternatives)" are shown, detailing their characteristics and price: "1 Pink, 32 MB, immediate, 120$", "2 Blue, 16 MB, immediate, 120$", "3 Black, 32 MB, 1 week, 150$", and "4 Red, 64 MB, 4 weeks, 150$". The screen then transitions to illustrate the AHP process, titled "AHP", with the first step highlighted: "Structure elements in criteria, sub-criteria, alternatives etc.". A hierarchical diagram appears, showing the "Objective" "Gadget to buy" at the top, branching into "Criteria" (Color, Memory, Delivery), and then further branching into "Sub-Criteria" (the specific colors, memory sizes, and delivery times). The second step of AHP is then highlighted: "Compare all elements pair wise with respect to the objective". A scale for comparison is introduced, ranging from "9" to "1/9", with "1" signifying "equal" importance, and "9" or "1/9" signifying "extreme" importance, with intermediate values representing "moderate strong", "strong", and "very strong". The speaker then demonstrates three pairwise comparisons: first, comparing "Color" and "Memory", where "Memory is 3 times more important than Color", resulting in a value of "3^-1" (1/3) for Color relative to Memory. Second, comparing "Color" and "Delivery", where "Delivery is 2 times more important than Color", resulting in "1/2" for Color relative to Delivery. Third, comparing "Memory" and "Delivery", where "Memory is equal important to Delivery", resulting in "1". Finally, a formula "(n^2 - n) / 2" is shown, explaining that for "n = 3" criteria, "3 results in 3 comparisons" are needed.

The video segment starts with a light blue background, displaying a dark green horizontal bar at the top with "AHP" written in white. Below this, a yellow horizontal bar contains the text "Arrange the result in a matrix with respect to the objective" (Arrange the result in a matrix with respect to the objective). Three light brown vertical blocks labeled "Color," "Memory," and "Delivery" are aligned horizontally at the top, representing criteria. Three light brown horizontal blocks, also labeled "Color," "Memory," and "Delivery," are stacked vertically on the left. As the video progresses, a 3x3 matrix is formed by populating cells with values: first the diagonal with '1's, then other cells with values like '3^-1', '1/2', '3', '1', and '2', representing pairwise comparisons between the criteria. Text appears at the bottom stating "and compute the normalized principal Eigen vector of the matrix" (and compute the normalized principal Eigen vector of the matrix), indicating the next step in the AHP process. The scene then transitions to a new slide with a dark gray title bar reading "Find the Eigen vector of the matrix" (Find the Eigen vector of the matrix). Below this, mathematical formulas are displayed, outlining how to calculate the matrix N for n=3 criteria, the sum of columns, and the normalized principal Eigen vector x1. Large green text, "Excel Sheet available," is prominently displayed in the center. Further formulas for calculating the largest Eigen value (λ), Consistency Index (CI), and Consistency Ratio (CR) are introduced, along with the instruction "Verify Consistency Ratio < 10%." A table titled "Random Index RI" showing values for 'n' from 1 to 10 appears at the bottom. The video then transitions to a result screen, again with "AHP" at the top and "Result:" (Result:) in a yellow bar. A hierarchical diagram shows "Gadget to buy" as the main objective, branching into three criteria: "Color 17%", "Memory 43%", and "Delivery 40%," displaying their calculated weights. Below this, a visual representation of "Criteria:" and "Weight:" blocks appears, with "Color" (blue block) next to "17%" (orange block), "Memory" (dark blue block) next to "43%" (orange block), and "Delivery" (light brown block) next to "40%" (orange block). Finally, a "Rank:" column appears, showing "1" for Memory, "2" for Delivery, and "3" for Color, indicating their relative importance.

The video segment illustrates the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) for decision-making. It opens with a slide displaying "AHP" in a green banner at the top, followed by a yellow box stating, "Compare all elements **pair wise** with respect to the objective." Below this, a blue box labeled "Gadget to buy" represents the overall objective. This objective branches into three main criteria: "Color 17%", "Memory 43%", and "Delivery 40%", each in a blue rectangular box. Under the "Color" criterion, five orange rectangular boxes list different sub-criteria or alternatives: "pink," "blue," "green," "black," and "red." A red rectangle then highlights these five color options. The scene then transitions, showing these color options transformed into 3D block-like representations, organized for pairwise comparisons. "pink" is compared sequentially with "blue," "green," "black," and "red," indicated by an arrow pointing from "pink" to a stack of the other colors. Similarly, "blue" is compared with "green," "black," and "red"; "green" with "black" and "red"; and "black" with "red." As the explanation progresses, numerical values representing the relative preference in each pairwise comparison are introduced in small orange blocks between the compared items. For example, "pink" vs. "blue" shows "2," and "pink" vs. "green" shows "3." By the end of the segment, all pairwise comparison values are displayed: "pink" is rated "2" over "blue," "3" over "green," "½" over "black," and "¼" over "red." "blue" is rated "3" over "green," "¼" over "black," and "⅓" over "red." "green" is rated "1/7" over "black" and "1/7" over "red." Finally, "black" is rated "⅓" over "red." A yellow text box appears in the bottom right corner, summarizing: "n = 5 results in 10 comparisons."

The video displays an instructional slide about the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) against a light blue background. Initially, the text "AHP" is at the top left, followed by a yellow box with "Arrange the result in a matrix" (Arrange the result in a matrix). Below this, a 5x5 matrix is shown, with columns and rows labeled "pink," "blue," "green," "black," and "red," containing numerical and fractional values (e.g., 1, 2, 3, 1/2, 1/4). A blue rectangle then highlights the entire matrix as new text appears below: "and compute the normalized principal Eigen vector of the matrix" (and compute the normalized principal Eigen vector of the matrix). The scene transitions to a hierarchical diagram with "Gadget to buy" at the top, branching into main criteria: "Color 17%", "Memory 43%", and "Delivery 40%." Under "Color," sub-criteria "pink 13%", "blue 12%", "green 5%", "black 22%", and "red 49%" are listed, and these percentages are briefly highlighted by a red box. The text in the yellow box changes to "Result:" (Result:). The next instruction appears: "Weight sub-criteria according weights of main-criteria" (Weight sub-criteria according weights of main-criteria). The "Color" sub-criteria now show an additional percentage column (e.g., "pink 13% 2.2%"), with these new values highlighted in a red box. Finally, the text in the yellow box changes to "Complete Result:" (Complete Result:), and the full hierarchical diagram is displayed. The "Memory" and "Delivery" branches are now also expanded with sub-criteria and two sets of percentages (e.g., "32 MB 43% 19%" under "Memory," and "one week 43% 17%" under "Delivery"). Various parts of this complete diagram are highlighted with quick red boxes, illustrating the final weighted alternatives.

The video opens with a light blue background featuring a green bar labeled "AHP" at the top, and below it, a yellow box stating "Evaluate alternatives." A hierarchical diagram titled "Gadget to buy" is central, branching into three main criteria: "Color (17%)", "Memory (43%)", and "Delivery (40%)". Each criterion has sub-options with associated percentages, for example, under "Color," "pink (13% 2.2%)," "blue (12% 2.0%)," "green (5% 0.8%)," "black (22% 3.7%)," and "red (49% 8.3%)." Similarly, "Memory" lists "8 MB (5% 2%)," "16 MB (7% 3%)," "32 MB (43% 19%)," and "64 MB (44% 19%)," while "Delivery" shows "immediate (46% 18%)," "one week (43% 17%)," and "4 weeks (12% 5%)." Below this diagram, a table named "Alternatives" lists four models with their specifications and a "Benefit" percentage. The video demonstrates the calculation for "Model 1 (Pink, 32 MB, immediate)": a red box highlights "Model 1," then "pink" (2.2%), "32 MB" (19%), and "immediate" (18%) are successively outlined in red. An animated golden box appears, displaying the summation "2% + 19%", which then updates to "2% + 19% + 18% = 39%," matching the "Benefit" value for Model 1 in the table. The video then shows the "Benefit" column for all models highlighted in red, indicating that similar calculations were done for them. Finally, a dark blue box appears at the bottom right, stating "Model 3 has the highest ranking," highlighting that it has the highest "Benefit" at 40%. The scene then transitions to a man with glasses wearing a white shirt, speaking in front of the partially visible previous slide.

A man with short hair and glasses, wearing a white collared shirt, speaks directly to the camera, gesturing slightly. Red text appears on screen, first stating "Price not taken as criterion" and then "separating benefits from costs allows for a". The scene then transitions to a presentation slide overlaid on the man's face, displaying a grid graph titled "AHP – cost vs. benefit". The Y-axis is labeled "Benefit" (with an upward arrow) ranging from 20% to 45%, and the X-axis is labeled "relative Costs" (with a rightward arrow) ranging from 20% to 30%. The red text "cost-benefit analysis" appears below the graph. The man's image fades, revealing the full slide. A table titled "Alternatives" appears below the graph, listing four models with their specifications (e.g., "Model 1: Pink, 32 MB, immediate") and corresponding "Benefit", "Cost $", and "Cost (norm)" values. Blue rectangles highlight the "Benefit" column, then the "Cost $" and "Cost (norm)" columns in the table, corresponding to the axes of the graph. Subsequently, four orange, numbered, 3D-rendered ellipses representing each model are plotted on the graph, one by one. Model 1 (39% Benefit, 22% relative Costs) appears in the top-left, Model 2 (23% Benefit, 22% relative Costs) in the bottom-left, Model 3 (40% Benefit, 28% relative Costs) in the top-right, and Model 4 (32% Benefit, 28% relative Costs) in the middle-right. As each model is plotted, its "Benefit" and "Cost (norm)" values in the table are highlighted in blue.

The video segment begins with a light blue background displaying a scatter plot titled "AHP - cost vs. benefit". The x-axis is labeled "relative Costs" (ranging from 20% to 30%), and the y-axis is labeled "Benefit" (ranging from 20% to 45%). Four data points, represented as numbered 3D cylinders, are visible on the grid. Initially, Model 1 (dark blue, at approximately 22% relative cost and 38% benefit) and Model 3 (dark blue, at approximately 28% relative cost and 39% benefit) are highlighted, while Models 2 and 4 are light yellow. An arrow then appears, pointing from Model 1 to Model 3, emphasizing a comparison between them. Concurrently, a text box appears at the bottom of the screen stating, "Model 3 has similar benefits compared to model 1, but higher costs. Probably you would go for model 1 with immediate delivery and lower price." (This text explains that Model 3 offers comparable benefits to Model 1 but at a greater cost, implying that Model 1 would be the preferred choice due to its lower price and immediate delivery). Following this, Models 1 and 3 revert to light yellow, and Models 2 (dark blue, at approximately 22% relative cost and 25% benefit) and 4 (dark blue, at approximately 28% relative cost and 31% benefit) become highlighted. The arrow and the previous text box vanish. A new arrow appears, pointing from Model 2 to Model 4. Simultaneously, a new text box displays, "Model 4 has significant higher benefits than model 2. Probably you would go for model 4 accepting longer delivery and higher price" (This text indicates that Model 4 provides considerably greater benefits than Model 2, suggesting it would be chosen despite potential trade-offs like longer delivery times and higher prices). Finally, the highlighted Models 2 and 4, the arrow, and the text box disappear. The chart remains on the screen as a semi-transparent man wearing glasses and a white collared shirt, with short brown hair, appears superimposed, looking at the camera and speaking.

A man with short hair and glasses, wearing a white collared shirt, is speaking directly to the camera against a plain light-colored wall. As he speaks, red text appears on the screen: first "evaluate product features" (0:06), then "select from strategic alternatives" (0:09), followed by "select KPIs" (0:13), "make consolidated decisions" (0:16), "with multiple inputs" (0:20), and finally "from different stakeholders" (0:21). The scene then transitions to a light blue background with blue text that reads, "Much learning does not teach understanding!" (0:25), "Business Performance Management" (0:27), "Klaus Goepel" (0:28), and "Singapore 2010" (0:29).
